desc: Implementation of the GNU pic "little language"
why: Pic is a 1980s little language for drawing diagrams in text; a close call since it is a niche typesetting tool with a retro charm.

brief.what_it_is: dpic is an implementation of the pic "little language", a text-based notation for describing diagrams that gets compiled into drawings. The homepage says it supports output to LaTeX, PDF, SVG, PostScript, and xfig 3.2. The homepage and GitLab project page I could load did not show the input format or a worked example, so I could not confirm the exact input-to-output workflow beyond that.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no stated rationale. The GitLab description frames it as an implementation of the pic little language with several output back ends. The brew scout note describes pic as a 1980s language for drawing diagrams in text, but that comes from the scout notes, not from the project pages I read.
brief.install_notes: Source is distributed as dpic.tar.gz or dpic.zip (version 2025.08.01) from the homepage, with a git repository at https://gitlab.com/aplevich/dpic. The homepage says a PC executable compiled with MinGW gcc is available. Beyond that I saw no build or configuration steps; the README and manual were not reachable from my fetches.
brief.standout: It is a modern, actively distributed implementation of a long-lived text-diagram language, and it can emit several formats (LaTeX, PDF, SVG, PostScript, xfig) from the same source. Those details come from the project description; I did not verify them against the README.
brief.status: Maintained, as far as I can tell: the homepage lists source downloads for version 2025.08.01 and a changelog, and the GitLab repo has a CHANGELOG. I did not see a last-commit date. The GitLab page says the project was created April 04, 2018.
brief.caveats: The README itself was not readable through my fetches. The GitLab blob URL I tried returned only a generic Files page, and the homepage's README link did not expose a URL I could follow. So the what_it_is, how_it_works, and commands sections rest on thin evidence. License and platform details beyond the MinGW Windows executable were not seen. The homepage was reachable.
quotes: An implementation of the pic "little language," with support for LaTeX, PDF, SVG, Postscript, and xfig 3.2 output.

entry.title: dpic
entry.tldr: dpic compiles pic, a small text language for describing diagrams, into SVG, PDF, PostScript, LaTeX or xfig drawings.
entry.deeper_look:
dpic is an implementation of pic, a "little language" for drawing diagrams from a text description. You write the diagram as source, and dpic compiles it into a drawing. The homepage lists output for LaTeX, PDF, SVG, PostScript and xfig 3.2, so one source file can feed several toolchains.

Pic comes from the 1980s Unix typesetting world, where documents were built from small tools that each did one job in a pipe. The idea is that a diagram is a program: you describe the shapes and how they relate, and the layout follows. That makes diagrams diffable, scriptable and easy to keep in version control.

The pages available for this entry did not show the input syntax or a worked example, so this entry does not describe the language itself. The manual linked from the homepage is the place to start. The project is still distributed: the homepage offers version 2025.08.01 with a changelog.
